 Judgment
For the injuries suffered in the road traffic accident, the claimant preferred claim petition before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Byadgi in MVC No.26 of 2017 seeking compensation.
2. Facts of the case in brief are that on 22nd June, 2016 the petitioner was travelling by car bearing registration No.KA- 27/M-9852 along with other inmates from Davanagere towards Ranebennur side.

The driver of the said car was driving the same in a high speed and rash and negligent manner and at about 4.30 pm, when the car came near Rajanahalli Jackwell on National Highway-4, the driver of the said car lost control over the car and hit the car to the road side bridge.

Consequently,
the car toppled.
Resultantly, the petitioner sustained injuries to all over the body.

Immediately, she was shifted to Government Hospital at Harihar where first-aid treatment was given and NC:
2023:KHC-D:10509-DB then she was shifted to SSIMS Hospital at Davanagere, thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to AJ Hospital and Research Center at Mangalore for higher treatment.

entities.text: AJ Hospital and Research Center at Mangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner has become physically disabled due to injuries sustained in the accident.

It is contended that prior to accident, she was hale and healthy and earning Rs.20,000/- per month by doing animal husbandry and due to the injuries sustained in the accident, she is unable to do any work and is unable to attend to her day-to-day chores and thereby lost her future earnings.
The respondents 1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending car and are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds she preferred the claim petition.

The Tribunal,
after hearing the arguments and considering the evidence on record, allowed the claim petition in Smt.Neela @ Neelaavva W/O Mallappa ... vs Yashavantha S/O Parasuram Patil on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45705911/
2 part and awarded compensation of Rs.12,59,398/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.

sentences.text:
Being not satisfied with the amount of compensation, the claimant is before this Court in this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
The learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has NC: 2023:KHC-D:10509-DB awarded meager compensation which is not commensurate to the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

The learned counsel submits considering the fact that the appellant has sustained 100% disability and completely bedridden, that too in her young age, the Tribunal ought to have considered adding future prospects at the rate of 40%.

To buttress his submission, he relies on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of JAGADISH V. MOHAN AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2018 SC 1347; and the judgment in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v.
PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

entities.text: JAGADISH V. MOHAN AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2018 SC 1347
entities.label: PRECEDENT

PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that the Tribunal has not awarded just and NC: 2023:KHC-D:10509-DB proper compensation on other heads.
On these grounds sought to enhance the compensation.

5. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Insurance Company sought to justify the impugned judgment and award and submits that the Tribunal, on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence placed before it, has awarded just and proper compensation and the same does not call for interference in this appeal and accordingly sought to dismiss the appeal.

6. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the records, the following points would arise for our consideration in this appeal:
1.
Whether the appellant has made out the ground for enhancement of compensation?
2. What order or award?

7. Our answer for the above points are as under:
Point No.1: in the affirmative;

3 Point No.2: as per final order.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10509-DB Regarding Point No.1:
8.
We have carefully examined the material placed before us.

In paragraphs 10 to 14, the Tribunal has given its finding as under:
"10.

The petitioner in order to prove her case has got examined herself as PW-1, and got examined the doctor as PW-2, and got marked the documents as Ex.P-1 to 21.
11.
The petitioner who has got examined herself as PW-1 has filed her affidavit in lieu of her oral chief examination.
The said PW-1 has reiterated all the contents of her petition in her affidavit.

The PW-1 has deposed that the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car and in said accident she has sustained injuries.
12.
The PW-2 is doctor.
The PW-2 is examined through court commissioner.

The PW-2 has deposed that he has examined the petitioner and he found permanent physical disability on the petitioner and he has issued disability certificate as per Ex.P-17.
13.
The petitioner in support of her case has relied upon the documents of Ex.P-1 to 21.
The Ex.P-1 is FIR.
Ex . P-2
is complaint.
Ex . P-3
is Final hospital bill.
Ex . P-4
is patient medical records of A.J. Hospital and Research Center.
Ex . P-5
is patient records of SSIMS and Research Center, Davanagere.
Ex . P-6
is charge sheet filed against NC: 2023:KHC-D:10509-DB the driver of the offending car for offences U/sec. 279, 337, 338 and 304 (A) of IPC.
Ex . P-7
is spot panchanama.
Ex . P-8
is IMV report.
Ex .P-9 is hand sketch map.
Ex .P-10 is driving license of the driver of the offending car.
Ex .P- 11 is Adhaar card of the petitioner.
Ex .P-12 is wound certificate.
Ex.P-13 are discharge summaries in 3 numbers.
Ex . P-14
are medical bills in 458 numbers.
Ex . P- 15 are prescriptions in 43 numbers.
Ex .P-16 are attender payment receipts in 18 numbers.
Ex .P-17 is disability certificate of the petitioner.
Ex. P-18
and 19
are patient medical records of AJ Institute of Medical Sciences, Mangalore.

entities.text: AJ Institute of Medical Sciences, Mangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Ex.P-20
is X-ray.
Ex.P-21 is medical bill."
14. The Ex.P-1 to 21 documents are in support of evidence of the PW-1 and 2.
The charge sheet which has been got marked as Ex.P-6 clearly reveals that the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Likewise, in charge sheet, it has been mentioned that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Likewise, the Ex.P-12 and 17 which are wound certificate and disability certificate of the petitioner reveal that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident."

9. Though the Tribunal observed in its judgment that the petitioner cannot stand up and was presented before the Court on wheel-chair and the lower limbs of the petitioner are paralysed and Smt.Neela @ Neelaavva W/O Mallappa ... vs Yashavantha S/O Parasuram Patil on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45705911/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: she has sustained 100% disability as per Exhibit P17-disability certificate issued by PW2 Doctor, but has NC: 2023:KHC-D:10509-DB assessed the disability at 33.33% and the Tribunal has not assigned any reason for not assessing the disability as per medical evidence.
The learned counsel for the appellant has requested this Court to examine the physical condition of the petitioner through video conferencing.
Accordingly, we have examined the appellant who has appeared through video conferencing.

On examination of the physical condition of the appellant and also considering the medical records and the observation made by the Tribunal in the impugned judgment and award, it is just and proper to assess the disability of the petitioner at 100%.
It is not in dispute that the age of the petitioner was 33 years as on the date of accident and she was doing animal husbandry.
Though it is averred in the claim petition, but no document was produced to show her income.

Therefore,
the Tribunal assessed the income of the claimant at Rs.8,000/- per month.
The same is not in consonance with the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
For the accidents of the year 2016, the notional income is to be taken at Rs.8,750/- per month and the same is taken in this case also.
As per the dictum of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of PRANAY SETHI (supra) 40% is to NC: 2023:KHC-D:10509-DB be added towards future prospects.

Hence,
the monthly income would be Rs.12,250/-.
As the deceased was aged 33 at the time of accident, the appropriate multiplier would be 16 and the same is adopted by the Tribunal.

Accordingly, the loss of future earning capacity would be Rs.23,52,000/- (Rs.12,250/- x 12 x 16 x 100%).
10.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the petitioner is aged 33 years and in view of the same, he prays for awarding suitable compensation towards attendant charges.

At this juncture, it is pertinent to refer to the dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of KAJAL v.
JAGDISH CHAND reported in (2020) 4 SCC 413, wherein it is observed thus:
"It would be apposite at this stage to refer to the observation of Lord Reid in Taylor v.
O'Connor:
"Damages to make good the loss of dependency over a period of years must be awarded as a lump sum and that sum is generally calculated by applying a multiplier to the amount of one year's dependency.

entities.text:
KAJAL v.
JAGDISH CHAND reported in (2020) 4 SCC 413
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That is a perfectly good method in the ordinary case but it conceals the fact that there are two quite separate matters involved, the present value of the series of future payments, and the discounting of that present value to allow for the fact that for one reason or another the person receiving the damages - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10509-DB might never have enjoyed the whole of the benefit of the dependency.
It is quite unnecessary in the ordinary case to deal with these matters separately.
Judges and counsel have a wealth of experience which is an adequate guide to the selection of the multiplier and any expert evidence is rightly discouraged.

But in a case where the facts are special, I think, that these matters must have separate consideration if even rough justice is to be done and expert evidence may be valuable or even almost essential.

The special factor in the present case is the Smt.Neela @ Neelaavva W/O Mallappa ... vs Yashavantha S/O Parasuram Patil on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45705911/
5 incidence of Income Tax and, it may be, surtax."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

11. Further at paragraphs 24 and 25 of the said judgment, it is observed thus:
"24.

This Court has reaffirmed the multiplier method in various cases like Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Subhagwati 10 1971 AC 115 and Others, U.P. State Road Transport Corporation and Others V. Trilok Chandra and Others, Sandeep Khanjuja v. Atul Dande.

entities.text: Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Subhagwati 10 1971 AC 115 and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: U.P. State Road Transport Corporation and Others V. Trilok Chandra and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has also recognised that Schedule II of the Act can be used as a guide for the multiplier to be applied in each case.
Keeping the claimant's age in mind, the multiplier in this case should be 18 as opposed to 44 taken by the High Court.
25. Having held so, we are clearly of the view that the basic amount taken for determining attendant charges is very much on the lower side.
We must remember that this little girl is severely suffering from incontinence meaning that she does not have control over her bodily functions like passing urine and faeces.

As she grows older,
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10509-DB she will not be able to handle her periods.
She requires an attendant virtually 24 hours a day.
She requires an attendant who though may not be medically trained but must be capable of handling a child who is bed ridden.
She would require an attendant who would ensure that she does not suffer from bed sores.
The claimant has placed before us a notification of the State of Haryana of the year 2010, wherein the wages for skilled labourer is Rs.4846/ per month.

We,
therefore, assess the cost of one attendant at Rs.5,000/- and she will require two attendants which works out to Rs.10,000/- per month, which comes to Rs.1,20,000/-
per annum, and using the multiplier of 18 it works out to Rs.21,60,000/- for attendant charges for her entire life.

This takes care of all the pecuniary damages."
12.

In the above said case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, considering the tender age of child, the difficulty of the child in handling her periods, so also considering her marriage prospects, opined that the claimant, in the said case, require two attendants and accordingly, considering Rs.5,000/-
per attendant, has awarded Rs.10,000/- per month towards attendant charges for the entire life.
In the case on hand, since the claimant is aged 33 years, we deem it appropriate that the one attendant would suffice to take care of the appellant.
Accordingly, the amount towards attendant charges would be Rs.9,60,000/- (Rs.5,000/- x 12 x 16).
The Tribunal has - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10509-DB awarded an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
Since this court has taken the disability of the claimant at 100%, the claimant is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
